intended_object: A positive definite matrix: a Hermitian square matrix M with xᴴ M x > 0 for every nonzero vector x (from the docstring and module documentation).
explanation: The definition requires M to be Hermitian, and the double sum Σᵢ Σⱼ star(xᵢ) · Mᵢⱼ · xⱼ (that is, xᴴ M x) to be strictly positive for every nonzero finitely supported vector x. When n is finite every vector is finitely supported, so this is exactly the textbook definition. Using finitely supported vectors also lets the definition make sense for infinite index types, where a sum over all of n could not be formed. The ring R only needs a star operation and a partial order, and the products are written as star(xᵢ) · Mᵢⱼ · xⱼ, so R need not be commutative; this is the natural generality. The definition matches its docstring. I know of no more general version in Mathlib, so the counterpart is left empty.
